notes: Building and Engineering News, vol. 17 part 1 (Internet Archive buildingengineer1717cont), the 26 weekly issues from 3 January to 27 June 1917. Same method as the later volumes: every numbered entry under Building Permit Applications and Building Contracts was taken from the djvu.xml OCR, East Bay headings set aside, and each San Francisco lot built from the block corner on the DPW street centrelines and compared with the sf-parcels shapes; a placement was accepted where the lot starts within two feet of a lot line of today (or the record names an unambiguous corner) and the roll dates the building 1916-1919, and alterations were matched by printed street number in sf-eas-addresses where the roll dates the building before 1917. The labels are printed with leader dots and each item is printed once. Every published row was read against the page image, location first; a cost or name that could not be read on the image was left out, and entries cut by a column break were read on in the next column. Descriptions of rows marked confidence low were built from the OCR and have not been read against the image. Owners are private individuals and are cut everywhere (raw.note; scrub_owner.py removes the fragments the OCR garbles past the first cut); a firm or institution named as owner is kept, and where the contractor, architect or designer named is the owner, shares the owner's surname or is listed at the owner's own address that name is cut too. Sub-trade contracts are timeline entries and set no builder credit; credits set from a garage or foundation listing were taken off again (3 25th Avenue, 2974 Pacific Avenue, the builder at 3630 Jackson Street). Completion notices, liens, sub-contracts printed 'on above' and the news columns were not taken. The paper came out on Wednesdays; issue dates are set from the cover dates (issues.json beside the corpus: first leaf of each issue, set by hand from the cover line or from the masthead four leaves after it), and the item numbers rise issue by issue under those dates. Item numbers run on from 1916 in the first issue (to 3,700) and restart with the issue of 10 January. One single house that was read against the image and has no name left to publish sits with the held single houses. Two held facts of other volumes whose parcels got a page from this volume were read: a July 1917 heating contract at 1214 29th Avenue was published in its own file, and a 1920 sun porch at 1745 Washington Street stays held because the roll gives apartments.

coverage.remaining: Vols. 17 pt. 1 to 31 read (January 1917 to January 1932); the 4 half-year volumes before 1917 (1915 and 1916) are unread, buildingengineer16916cont next. In this volume: 116 rows placed on a parcel whose roll year fits, single houses with no architect named and no page, are logged and held until another fact gives the parcel a page (extra.placed_apn; all but one still need the image check). 319 rows have a nearest parcel that was not accepted (the lot starts off today's lot lines, or the roll dates the building outside the window). 577 rows were not placed: location lines not parsed (tract lots, garbled headings), street pairs that do not cross under the names read, and printed street numbers with no EAS row today.
coverage.note: 2,013 numbered entries read, 1,147 San Francisco rows, 570 placed on a parcel, 136 picked and read against the page image, 103 published on 98 pages (50 seeded), 32 held back: 18 storeys, unit counts or uses that contradict the roll, 11 alterations with nothing to confirm the street number and three pieces of minor work; one more joined the held houses.
